title: Piston Pump

introduction.definition: A reciprocating piston pump uses a piston with seals moving back and forth in a cylinder liner; suction and discharge check valves make the flow one-way. Double-acting designs pump on both strokes. Flow is proportional to speed and stroke and nearly independent of pressure, but it pulsates.
key_points: Double-acting duplex piston pump in the model
Valves are the main wear part
introduction.summary: A piston pump moves liquid with a piston that slides in a cylinder liner, sealed against the bore by elastomer cups on the piston itself. In the double-acting design shown, both faces of the piston work: as it travels one way, the chamber ahead of it discharges while the chamber behind it fills, and the roles reverse on the return stroke. Two cylinders cranked 90° apart (duplex) give four deliveries per revolution. Used for drilling mud, slurries and general high-pressure transfer at moderate pressures.

piping: Pulsation dampeners on suction and discharge.
Short, large suction; acceleration head must be included in NPSHa.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
commissioning: Never start against a closed discharge valve.
Fill the pump with liquid (or ensure the suction is flooded) before start — avoid dry running unless the design allows it.

routine.task: Check packing leakage and crankcase oil.

video_tutorials.title: Piston Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Piston Pump.
A reciprocating piston pump uses a piston with seals moving back and forth in a cylinder liner; suction and discharge check valves make the flow one-way.
Double-acting designs pump on both strokes.
Flow is proportional to speed and stroke and nearly independent of pressure, but it pulsates.
Typical applications include mud pumps for drilling; high-pressure water and process injection; pipeline and slurry transport (piston/plunger diaphragm); hydraulic test benches.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Piston Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Piston Pump.
Check packing leakage and crankcase oil.
Inspect valves and seats.
Replace liners and piston seals.
Watch for valve wear: loss of flow, knocking. Common cause: abrasives, cavitation.
Watch for pulsation / pipe vibration: shaking pipework. Common cause: no/ineffective dampener.
Watch for cavitation from acceleration head: knocking on suction. Common cause: long suction line.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: What makes the flow one-way in a piston pump?
"Double-acting" means…
options: The piston pumps on both strokes
questions.explanation: Both sides of the piston work.

questions.question: Why are pulsation dampeners used?
options: To smooth the pulsating flow and reduce pipe vibration

questions.question: Acceleration head on the suction side…
options: Reduces available NPSH and must be included
questions.explanation: Accelerating the suction column costs pressure.
